text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: runtime-prod GPU OOMs detected. 3 hosts reporting OOM signals, service=runtime, severity=sev2. Creating thread for live triage — <https://internal.incidents/4512345678|incident page>

sam - oncall: Ack, I'm on it. Tailing logs and metrics now. pinging @maria for GPU mem graphs.

maria: pulling metrics — GPU free dropped ~8GB -> ~600MB between 15:22-15:24 UTC on hosts i-021,i-022,i-023. Per-token allocations spike aligns with increased avg sequence length. quick graph: <https://graphs.internal/gpu-mem/4512345678>

alex: any recent rollouts? I see a model push v3.3 at 14:58 across prod (canary then ramp).

sam - oncall: timeline so far: rollout v3.3 @14:58 -> errors start ~15:22. Hypothesis A: model behavior increase KV/attention state growth; Hypothesis B: longer sequences causing fragmentation.

jinx (incidents-bot): Customer-impact summary: ~4% of requests returned 502/timeout between 15:22-15:38. ~10 customers surfaced elevated latency. Dashboard: <https://dash/reports/4512345678>

ellie: kicking quick mitigation: reducing batch_size on pool-B from 16 -> 8 to lower transient alloc pressure. Command I used: ```
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/pools/pool-B/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"inference": {"batch_size": 8}}'
```

tao: enabling more aggressive eviction on model-cache on hosts i-021,i-022. Applied eviction policy=LRU+pin-threshold=0.6 at 15:26.

sam - oncall: Applied ellie's batch-size change at 15:27. Observing allocation rate drop on pool-B. Will confirm for pools A/C next.

maria: mem trend starting to level at 15:31 for pool-B. Host i-022 still shows a fatal allocation failure at 15:29; dmesg+alloc traces uploaded: <https://logs.internal/4512345678/i-022/dmesg.txt> and <https://logs.internal/4512345678/i-022/mem-trace.log>

alex: looking at traces — observed many small pinned allocations and scatter allocation pattern. Total free memory exists but no contiguous block large enough for some allocation attempts -> fragmentation. Host i-022 shows repeated page-faults during KV page evictions.

ellie: quick canary: capping max_sequence_length to 1024 for 5% of traffic (canary group) at 15:35 to limit KV growth.

sam - oncall: canary results positive so far (15:38): reduced mem growth on canary, fewer OOM traces. Rolling cap to 25% while we continue analysis.

jinx (incidents-bot): Update: mitigations applied, customer impact decreasing. Still monitoring for regressions.

tao: handoff to next oncall @tao at 15:45 — summary: rollout v3.3 correlated, mitigations (batch_size reduction, eviction tweak, seq_len cap) in place. Links: graphs/logs/dash above. I'll collect kernel traces and stitch a timeline.

tao: Proposed longer-term mitigations to evaluate: 1) revert v3.3 if RCA confirms model change is root cause, 2) introduce preemptive compaction of model-local KV pages, 3) make dynamic batch-sizing per-host based on free contiguous memory, 4) add fragmentation health metric to alerts.

alex: taking rca-owner. I'll produce timeline, hypothesis matrix (fragmentation vs kv-growth vs alloc churn), and confirm whether v3.3 changed attention/cache layout or increased key sizes. Will coordinate with model-team.

sam - oncall: leaving detailed notes in the incident ticket and handoff checklist. Thanks all — please add any missing logs or customer notes into the ticket. :thumbsup:

jinx (incidents-bot): Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem required. Assigned: alex (RCA). Action items: collect full kernel traces, confirm model diffs, run stress repro on staging with v3.3 to validate fragmentation.
